newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Delay in refloating Torres Strait grounded vessel.
newsitem.headline: Delay in refloating Torres Strait grounded vessel.

text.p: Australian maritime safety officials said attempts to refloat a 47,000-tonne bulk coal carrier aground in Torres Strait have been delayed until Tuesday morning when a rescue tug was expected to be at the scene.
It was earlier hoped the Bombay-registered Dakshineshwar would refloat on a high tide on Monday night after hitting a sandbank off Wednesday Island, late on Saturday night, officials said.

Queensland Transport maritime spokeman John Watkinson said the ship's master on Sunday night acknowledged his instruction not to attempt a refloat until the tug from Port Moresby was in place and other safety conditions met.
The tug had been delayed by customs in Port Moresby and would not arrive until early Tuesday morning, Watkinson said.

Martitime Safety authorities said earlier, the vessel, enroute from Hay Point near Gladstone to India with a full cargo, had suffered engine failure and steering problems but there was no imminent danger of an oil spill.
The ship's master was organising an inspection of the hull to double-check its condition, given the sensitive environment, he said.
"Conditions will be favourable for some days yet and as the vessel is secure, the ship's master has time to make a commercial decision about choosing a tug salvor," Watkinson said.
